proposals.evidence: DEDR 3986(a) documents the pal tooth family: Kodagu pallï, Malayalam pallu, Tamil pal, Malto palu, Kolami pal, Gadaba pal/pallū with plural palkīl, and Toda pas̱. Survey plural and final-vowel material (including palku, pālkill, pāldu) remains unchanged. Toda parse is a comparative correspondence to its distinctive s̱ reflex; Betta Kurumba pallə extends the comparison to a lect absent from this article. Subsection (b) toothstick compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5517 explicitly gives Kannada beṅki fire, Malto béru sun, Brahui bāsing become hot and Ollari Gadaba veytal hot (in veytal nīr hot water). The source annotation identifies the family; survey benki, bērdu, bāsun and veṭal preserve their consonant and ending differences. The Gadaba survey response is the heat word alone, so no water component is inferred. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2598 gives Kolami sī- with past sīt-, Kurukh ciʾinā, Malto ciye and Gadaba sī- give. Source cognacy identifies the family. Survey sītān, cihna, cibāh and ci preserve their inflection and transcriptions; the final material is not removed to simulate a literal dictionary match. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4240 directly gives Kota peg and Ollari Gadaba pog smoke, alongside Kannada poge and the wider pukai family. Survey pegu/poāg retain their final-vowel and vowel-sequence differences. Betta Kurumba pəggi is a comparative extension explicitly only a look-alike in the source, not a literal dictionary attestation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
